goal: On a successful SimBrief import (a real new planned_legs row, not the duplicate short-circuit), automatically file one 'dispatch' category ACARS message into that leg's thread summarizing route/cruise altitude/fuel/alternates/ETE, sourced from the already-fetched SimBrief response. Add a load-sheet request/reply feature scoped to a planned leg (a new endpoint) that generates block fuel / payload / ZFW figures from that leg's SimBrief-sourced dispatch data and files a downlink request + uplink reply pair in the same thread. A leg with no dispatch data on file rejects the load-sheet request with exactly 'NO DISPATCH DATA ON FILE', no server error. Add the equivalent action to client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx (the MCDU client is out of scope, it lives in oshogun/msfslogger_mcdu).
frozen_decisions: Message direction convention: the pilot's request is downlink, the generated reply is uplink. Applies to the dispatch-release message (uplink, originates from dispatch) and to the load-sheet request/reply pair (request=downlink, reply=uplink). The weather story's opposite wording is a documented slip, not intentional, and is not to be followed.
SimBrief data is not re-fetched anywhere in this run. Fuel/ETE/payload/ZFW figures come only from the single fetchSimbriefPlan(userId) call already made in POST /trips/:id/planned-legs/simbrief.
No schema migration is expected. acars_messages already has payload_json, dedup_key, correlation_id and is explicitly scoped by planned_leg_id for the before-a-flights-row-exists case.
Frontend scope is this repo's own web client only (client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx). Wiring oshogun/msfslogger_mcdu is out of scope and not tracked as a follow-up here.
Payload/ZFW figures are illustrative, not a real performance calculation, and must not be presented as authoritative.
No new external integration; simbriefClient.ts remains the only source, called once per import as today.
Ship/DevOps phase is skipped: no build, packaging, deploy or CI file is touched by this run.
sequencing_rationale: This run introduces a contract change (ParsedSimbriefPlan's fuel/ETE fields or an equivalent raw-body pass-through) and a new endpoint whose payload_json shape a second route depends on reading back. Per the intake, Design must freeze both before any implementer opens a file, so Design is phase 1's first task and every implementation task in phase 1 depends on it.

Backend (dispatch emission + load-sheet endpoint, all in src/**) and frontend (the web client's load-sheet action, all in client/**) touch disjoint file sets and both only need the frozen contract, not each other's code, to proceed — so they are two parallel tasks in phase 1 rather than sequential phases. This mirrors the pattern used in 2026-09-11-tauri-windows-client (T-005/T-006 both depending on the design gate).

The backend task is kept as one task, not split by file: src/simbrief.ts (parser contract), src/routes/plannedLegs.ts (dispatch emission on import) and the load-sheet route are tightly coupled through the payload_json shape the writer produces and the reader depends on — splitting them risks the same inconsistency Design exists to prevent, and per cost discipline two edits that share a contract are one task.

A single phase is enough here: there is no user-visible seam between 'dispatch message exists' and 'load-sheet works' worth shipping separately, and Ship is skipped, so one design->implement->review phase covers the whole run.

phases.name: Dispatch release and load sheet
phases.ships: On every successful SimBrief import, a dispatch-release ACARS message appears automatically in the leg's thread with route/cruise altitude/fuel/alternates/ETE. A REQUEST LOADSHEET action in the web ACARS Messages page (client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx) files a downlink request and an uplink generated load sheet (block fuel, payload, ZFW) into the same thread when the leg has dispatch data on file, and is rejected with exactly "NO DISPATCH DATA ON FILE" (no server error) when it does not.

tasks.title: Freeze the SimBrief-contract change, the dispatch payload_json shape, and the load-sheet endpoint
tasks.goal: Produce .claude/runs/2026-09-14-acars-dispatch-loadsheet/design.md deciding and specifying, precisely enough that backend_sr and frontend_sr need nothing else: (1) how fuel/ETE reach the dispatch message without a second SimBrief fetch — either ParsedSimbriefPlan (src/simbrief.ts) gains typed fields read from the OFP's `fuel` and `times` nodes, or POST /trips/:id/planned-legs/simbrief retains the raw decoded body alongside `plan` and reads the extra fields itself; name the exact source fields (confirmed present in samples/simbrief/simbrief.userid.json: fuel.plan_ramp, fuel.plan_takeoff, fuel.plan_landing, fuel.taxi, fuel.enroute_burn, fuel.reserve, fuel.contingency, fuel.alternate_burn; times.est_time_enroute in seconds; weights.est_zfw, weights.payload, weights.oew) and which ones the dispatch message body/payload_json actually needs; (2) the exact payload_json shape written into the dispatch message at import time, sufficient for the load-sheet route to derive block fuel / payload / ZFW without recomputing from a raw SimBrief body, and the human-readable dispatch message body text (route, cruise altitude, planned fuel, alternates, ETE); (3) how a dispatch message is looked up for a leg (query by planned_leg_id + category='dispatch' via listAcarsMessagesForPlannedLeg, or a dedicated finder) and how insertAcarsMessageOnce's dedup_key is derived so exactly one dispatch message exists per leg even if the emission code runs twice (AC1); (4) the load-sheet endpoint contract: HTTP method/path (a planned-leg-scoped route, consistent with the existing POST /trips/:id/planned-legs/simbrief and GET/PATCH/DELETE /planned-legs/:legId in src/routes/plannedLegs.ts — decide whether it lives in that file or a new one), request body (none needed — the leg id in the path is the only input), success response shape (the two created messages, or an envelope naming both), the exact downlink request body text and uplink reply body text/fixed-field format, the dedup/re-request semantics (does re-requesting file a new pair every time, matching the existing canned-message route's 'no dedup, pressing twice files twice' precedent, or dedup like the dispatch message — pick one and say why), and the exact rejection path when no dispatch message is on file for the leg: HTTP status and the literal body "NO DISPATCH DATA ON FILE"; (5) the TypeScript types both sides need, named for both files that will carry them by hand (src/types.ts and client/src/types.ts, mirrored as AcarsMessage/AcarsThread already are) — a LoadsheetRequestResponse shape at minimum; (6) exactly where in POST /trips/:id/planned-legs/simbrief (src/routes/plannedLegs.ts:201-288) the dispatch-message write is inserted — after createPlannedLeg succeeds, never on the duplicate short-circuit path, and wrapped so a message-write failure logs but does not turn the 201 import response into an error. Confirm field names against the real sample before freezing, not just the interface comment.
acceptance_criteria: design.md names, for every new/changed field, the exact SimBrief JSON path it is read from, checked against samples/simbrief/simbrief.userid.json (`python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('samples/simbrief/simbrief.userid.json')); print(d['fuel'], d['times'], d['weights'])"` shows the fields named in the doc exist at those paths).
design.md states explicitly whether ParsedSimbriefPlan (src/simbrief.ts) gains new fields or the route retains the raw decoded body, and gives the exact new field names/types either way.

design.md specifies the dispatch message's payload_json as a concrete JSON shape (key names and types), and states the dedup_key formula used with insertAcarsMessageOnce so a second call for the same leg is a no-op, not a second row.
design.md gives the load-sheet endpoint's exact method, path, success response shape, downlink/uplink body text format, and the literal rejection body "NO DISPATCH DATA ON FILE" with its HTTP status.

design.md states the re-request semantics for the load-sheet endpoint (new pair every time, or deduped) and justifies the choice against the existing canned-message and PDC-dedup precedents already in the codebase.
design.md lists the exact TypeScript type names and shapes to add to src/types.ts and client/src/types.ts.

design.md states precisely where in src/routes/plannedLegs.ts the dispatch-message write is inserted, confirms it is unreachable from the duplicate short-circuit (the `if (!allowDuplicates) { ... return; }` block above the write), and confirms a message-write failure does not change the import route's success response or status code.

tasks.title: Emit the dispatch-release message on SimBrief import and add the load-sheet request/reply endpoint
tasks.goal: Per `ctx.sh design 2026-09-14-acars-dispatch-loadsheet <sections frozen by T-001 covering: SimBrief contract change, dispatch payload_json shape, dedup key, load-sheet endpoint contract, and insertion point>`: (1) extend src/simbrief.ts (or the import route, per the design's decision) so fuel/ETE data from the already-fetched SimBrief response is available without a second fetch; (2) in POST /trips/:id/planned-legs/simbrief (src/routes/plannedLegs.ts), after createPlannedLeg succeeds and only on that path (never on the `status: 'duplicate'` short-circuit), file exactly one `category: 'dispatch'`, `direction: 'uplink'` message into the new leg's thread via insertAcarsMessageOnce, with the payload_json and dedup_key the design specifies, summarizing route/cruise altitude/planned fuel/alternates/ETE in the body; a failure writing this message must be logged and must not change the import route's response or status; (3) add the load-sheet endpoint the design specifies (method/path/response), reading the leg's on-file dispatch message (via listAcarsMessagesForPlannedLeg, filtered to category='dispatch') to derive block fuel / payload / ZFW, filing a `direction: 'downlink'` request message and a `direction: 'uplink'` reply message as the design specifies (dedup or not, per its decision) into the same planned-leg-scoped thread; (4) when the leg has no dispatch message on file, respond with the design's exact rejection — the literal body "NO DISPATCH DATA ON FILE", no thrown/500 error; (5) add the TypeScript types the design names to src/types.ts.
acceptance_criteria: A scratch-server import of samples/simbrief/simbrief.userid.json onto a fresh trip (`curl -s -X POST localhost:<scratch-port>/api/trips/<id>/planned-legs/simbrief ...` against a userId that returns the sample, or a direct createPlannedLeg + emission call exercised via a small ts-node script) results in exactly one row in acars_messages with category='dispatch', planned_leg_id set to the new leg, direction='uplink', and a body containing the route, cruise altitude, planned fuel, alternates and ETE — verified with a better-sqlite3 query against the scratch db, not the live flights.db.

Re-running the same import against the duplicate-short-circuit path (same OFP, allow_duplicates not set) produces zero additional acars_messages rows — the dedup_key/insertAcarsMessageOnce guarantee holds even if emission code is invoked twice for the same leg.
`npx tsc --noEmit` passes with the ParsedSimbriefPlan/route change in place.

POST to the load-sheet endpoint for a leg that has the dispatch message on file returns 201 (or the design's chosen success status) with a response containing block fuel, payload and ZFW figures, and the acars thread for that leg (`listAcarsMessagesForPlannedLeg`) now has two additional rows: one direction='downlink' request and one direction='uplink' reply, both after the dispatch message in sent_at order.

POST to the load-sheet endpoint for a leg with no dispatch message on file (e.g. a leg imported via the .lnmpln route, which never emits one) returns a non-2xx response whose body is exactly "NO DISPATCH DATA ON FILE" and writes zero acars_messages rows — verified by a subsequent listAcarsMessagesForPlannedLeg query returning the same count as before the request.

The import route's success response (`imported`/`result` fields, 201 status) is unchanged when the dispatch-message write is forced to throw (e.g. temporarily point at a closed db handle in a scratch script) — the import still returns 201 with the created leg; only a console.error line differs.

Disable/hide or grey out the action when `plannedLegId` is null (no planned leg linked to this flight at all) consistent with how the page already treats missing planned-leg context. Surface the "NO DISPATCH DATA ON FILE" rejection as an inline error the same way `sendError` is shown today, not a thrown/uncaught exception.
